source_text: Renuntiemus carnalibus, ut aliquando spiritalia retractemus. Rape occasionem, etsi non exoptatissimam, attamen opportunam, non habere cui debitum solveres, et a quo exsolvereris: desiisti esse debitor. O te felicem! dimisisti debitorem; sustine damnum. Quid si, quod diximus damnum, lucrum sentias? Per continentiam enim negotiaberis magnam substantiam sanctitatis; parcimonia carnis, spiritum adquires. Recogitemus enim ipsam conscientiam nostram, quam alium se homo sentiat: cum forte a sua foemina cessat, spiritaliter sapit. Si orationem facit ad Dominum, prope est coelo. Si scripturis incumbit, totus illic est. Si psalmum canit, placet sibi. Si daemonem adjurat, confidit sibi. Ideo Apostolus temporalem purificationem orationum commendandarum caussa adjecit; ut sciremus, quod ad tempus prodest semper nobis exercendum esse, ut semper prosit. Quotidie, imo omni momento oratio hominibus necessaria est, utique et continentia, postquam oratio necessaria est. Oratio de conscientia procedit. Si conscientia erubescat, erubescit oratio. Spiritus deducit orationem ad Deum. Si spiritus reus apud se sit conscientiae erubescentis, quomodo audebit orationem ducere ab illa, de qua erubescente et ipse suffunditur sanctus minister? Etenim est prophetica vox veteris Testamenti: Sancti eritis, quia Deus sanctus; et rursus: Cum sancto sanctificaberis, et cum viro innocente innocens eris, et cum electo electus. Debemus enim ita ingredi in disciplina Domini, ut dignum est, non secundum carnis calentes concupiscentias. Ita enim et Apostolus dicit, quod sapere secundum carnem mors sit; secundum spiritum vero sapere vita aeterna sit in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Si haec obfusio, etiam cum in unis nuptiis res carnis exercetur, Spiritum Sanctum avertit, quanto magis cum in secundo matrimonio agitur?
pass_a_gloss: Let us renounce carnal things so that at some time we may reconsider spiritual things. Seize the opportunity, even if not the most desired, yet opportune, to not have someone to whom you owe a debt and from whom you are freed: you have ceased to be a debtor. Oh, you are fortunate! you have dismissed the debtor; endure the loss. What if, what we have called loss, you consider gain? For through continence you will indeed negotiate a great wealth of sanctity; by parsimony of the flesh, you acquire the spirit. Let us reconsider our own conscience, which a person feels to be different: when perhaps he ceases from his own wife, he has spiritual understanding. If he makes a prayer to the Lord, he is near heaven. If he devotes himself to the scriptures, he is entirely there. If he sings a psalm, it pleases him. If he adjures a demon, he trusts in himself. Therefore the Apostle added a temporary purification for the sake of commendable prayers; so that we may know what is profitable for a time to be always exercised by us, so that it may always be profitable. Every day, or rather every moment, prayer is necessary for people, and also continence, since prayer is necessary. Prayer proceeds from conscience. If conscience is ashamed, prayer is ashamed. The Spirit leads prayer to God. If the spirit is guilty before itself of a conscience that is ashamed, how will it dare to lead prayer from that which, being ashamed, even the holy minister is stained? Indeed, there is a prophetic voice of the Old Testament: You will be holy, because God is holy; and again: You will be sanctified with the holy, and with the innocent man you will be innocent, and with the elect you will be elect. For we ought to enter into the discipline of the Lord in such a way as is worthy, not according to the hot desires of the flesh. For thus also the Apostle says, that to think according to the flesh is death; but to think according to the spirit is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. If this obscuration, even when the fleshly thing is exercised in single marriage, averts the Holy Spirit, how much more when a second marriage is undertaken?

pass_b_english:
We must renounce carnal things so that at some point we may reconsider spiritual ones. Seize the opportunity, even if it is not the one you most desire, for it is still opportune: you no longer have anyone to whom you owe a debt, nor anyone from whom you might be freed; you have ceased to be a debtor. How fortunate you are! You have dismissed the debtor; now endure the loss. But what if what we call loss you experience as gain? For through continence you will indeed secure a great wealth of sanctity; by sparing the flesh, you acquire the spirit.

Let us re-examine our own conscience, which a person perceives as different from himself: when he happens to abstain from his own wife, he gains spiritual understanding. If he prays to the Lord, he is near heaven. If he devotes himself to the Scriptures, he is entirely there. If he sings a psalm, it pleases him. If he adjures a demon, he trusts in himself. Therefore the Apostle added a temporary purification for the sake of commendable prayers, so that we may know that what profits for a time must always be exercised by us, so that it may always profit. Prayer is necessary for human beings every day, indeed at every moment, and continence likewise, since prayer is necessary. Prayer proceeds from conscience. If conscience is ashamed, prayer is ashamed. The Spirit leads prayer to God. If the spirit stands guilty before itself because of a conscience that is ashamed, how will it dare to lead prayer from that very source, when even the holy minister is stained by its shame?

Indeed, there is a prophetic voice of the Old Testament: "You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy" (Leviticus 11:44); and again: "With the holy you show yourself holy, and with the innocent man you show yourself innocent, and with the elect you show yourself elect" (Psalm 18:26). For we ought to enter the discipline of the Lord in a manner worthy of him, not according to the hot desires of the flesh. For thus the Apostle also says that to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace in Christ Jesus our Lord (Romans 8:6). If this obscuration, even when the fleshly act is exercised within a single marriage, drives away the Holy Spirit, how much more when a second marriage is undertaken?

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and provides the necessary scripture citations for the Old Testament and Pauline allusions which were present in the Latin but lacked verse numbers in the source. Pass A is a faithful gloss. All clauses, agency, and theological distinctions are preserved.
